plot: It's a hundred degrees and you chug a bucket-sized cup of ice water. Gus the stomach gets hit by a cold front called Cubert, Cortez gets a pain call from the trigeminal nerve (brain freeze), Neff runs the water budget, and Cortez stamps DENIED on MAKE IT STOP. Twist: the brain can't feel pain itself. A second cup arrives and the stamp does nothing. Tease: leg day.

script.title: Your Organs When You Chug Ice Water on a 100°F Day

episode.action: chug ice water on a hot day

beats.title: Your Organs When You Chug Ice Water on a 100°F Day

beats.say: Weather report: a hundred degrees outside. Everybody drink something.
The thermostat in here says we're fine. The thermostat is lying.
Core temperature is ninety-eight point six. Barely holding on.
It's so hot, even the air is sweating!
Even my kidneys are sweating. I didn't know that was possible.
Sweat is on. Blood is rushing to the skin to dump heat.
beats.label: Sweat: evaporation cools the skin

beats.say: Sweat is good. Sweat is our friend. Let it flow.
Which means my budget is bleeding. Water out, nothing in.
Order of the day: water. Emergency water. Ice if possible.
I vote for something frozen. Maybe a slushie.
Nobody asked for your vote, Beat.
The eyes just spotted a gas station cup the size of a bucket!
Is that ice? That's mostly ice.
Mostly ice. It's basically a freezer with a straw.
Everybody brace. It's coming down the hatch.
Cold front! Cold front! Who ordered a blizzard?
Cubert. Ice cube. I'm cool. Technically.
Cubert? That sounds like a bad nickname.
Do you know what temperature this kitchen runs at?
A nice, comfy seventy?
Ninety-eight point six. You are thirty-two. Show some respect.
beats.label: Core temperature: held near 98.6°F

beats.say: I've never been this warm. It's overwhelming.
Welcome to the human body, kid.
Relax. My walls warm everything up fast. It's what I do.
Do you have a towel? I'm sweating. I'm melting. Same thing.
I think I'm getting smaller. Is that normal?
Every cold drink takes a short vacation here. Then it goes to work.
WHOA! Pain! Pain on line seven! Where's it coming from?!
The roof of the mouth! The cold hit it way too fast!
The roof of the mouth? Why is nobody guarding the roof?!
Is it my brain?! Is my brain freezing?!
Your brain can't feel pain, Cortez. Not on its own.
beats.label: Brain tissue: can't feel pain itself

beats.say: Then who is screaming at me?!
The trigeminal nerve. It carries face pain to your desk.
beats.label: Trigeminal nerve: carries face pain signals

beats.say: So my face is yelling at me. Great.
Should we breathe through it? In and out? In and out?
Yes. Slowly. Do not hyperventilate on me.
Scientists think blood vessels up here squeeze, then open wide.
Squeeze, then open. Like a bad zipper.
Memo: make it stop. Stamp it.
Good news. It usually fades in under a minute.
Never again. I'm writing it down. Never. Again.
Same speech every summer. Same stamp. Same result.
You say that every summer.
I'm almost water now! Small intestine, please take me in!
beats.label: Small intestine: absorbs most of your water

beats.say: Ready or not, bloodstream, here I come!
Cubert, please keep your elbows in.
More fluid in the pipes. Pressure's steady. I like it.
Everybody's so friendly! Hi, red blood cell! Hi, white blood cell!
Last words: I was a great ice cube.
Also, I owe the straw ten bucks.
You were a very cold ice cube.
Tell Gus I said thanks for the warm welcome.
Fresh water! My favorite delivery!
Neff, new rule. No more fresh water jokes.
That was my best one this week.
I filter about half a cup of blood every minute. All day.
beats.label: Kidneys: filter half a cup a minute

beats.say: How much of it do we send out?
A quart or two a day. Depends how much you drink.
So we need a restroom soon.
Not yet. Give me a few minutes. Quality control.
Everyone's an expert on restrooms today.
Also, you're roughly half to sixty percent water.
beats.label: Body water: about 50 to 60 percent

beats.say: So we're basically a very fancy cup.
A cup with opinions.
Wait. The eyes say there's a second cup. Same size.
Round two?! Already?!
This is why I never take a day off.
My pulse hasn't even recovered from round one!
I just finished the first batch.
Everyone, positions. We take this one slowly.
Stamp the memo. No more ice. Not ever.
Pretty sure the stamp doesn't work on you.
Hey! Is it cold again? Do I need a coat?
No. Wait. This one is room temperature. Aww, thank you.
Finally. Someone who respects the kitchen.
Heart rate is normal. Temperature is stable. I'm so proud of us.
Great teamwork. Gold stars for everyone. Except Neff.
What did I do?!
Nothing. That's the problem. I'm kidding. Maybe.
Cubert is now sweat, urine, or part of a blood cell. Respect.
We'll miss him. He was cool.
Moment of silence for the ice cube.
In. Out. In. Out. That's our silence.
Never again. Quote me.
Next time: leg day. Somebody call in sick for me.

fact.title: REAL BODY NOTE
lines: Kidneys filter half a cup of blood a minute.
fact.source: NIDDK: Your Kidneys & How They Work; OpenStax A&P 2e

long.description:
A hundred degrees outside, a cup the size of a bucket, and an ice cube named Cubert who just wanted a warm welcome. Gus gets hit by a cold front, Cortez fields an angry call from the trigeminal nerve, and Neff does the math on how much water your kidneys really handle.

Real body notes (sources): NIDDK, Your Kidneys & How They Work: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/kidney-disease/kidneys-how-they-work ; NIDDK, Your Digestive System & How It Works: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/digestive-system-how-it-works ; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e: https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e
Brain freeze mechanisms are still being studied; we describe the leading explanation.
Entertainment and general education, not medical advice. Original characters, animated in Blender. Made for adults and families, not made for kids.
